name: Vivek Ramaswamy
role: Businessman and author; 2024 Republican presidential candidate; 2026 Republican nominee for Ohio governor
summary: Ramaswamy is a conservative, America-first Republican who combines market-oriented economics with cultural conservatism and a restrictionist border policy. He favors deep cuts to the federal bureaucracy, fossil and nuclear energy, school choice and opposes affirmative action, DEI and ESG. On foreign policy he favors reducing involvement in Ukraine and NATO while focusing on China.

abolish-income-tax.rationale: His 2026 Ohio platform pledges to abolish and phase out the state income tax, starting with capital gains; for the federal level his 2023 campaign proposed a 12% flat income tax rather than abolition.

abolish-ip.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 4) defends the pharmaceutical patent bargain, high prices during the patent term and cheap generics afterwards, as a system that works; it does not address copyright.

abortion-legal.rationale: Says he is pro-life and that abortion is a form of murder; supports six-week state bans with exceptions for rape, incest and the woman's life, but opposes a national ban.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: He explains his vegetarian tradition through moral respect for animals while acknowledging hunters’ respect for wildlife.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 5) says he is vegetarian for religious and moral reasons and thinks it generally wrong to kill animals simply for culinary pleasure; he does not address animal research.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He explicitly says the executive cannot spend money Congress has not authorized.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 13) praises birthright citizenship as a powerful unifying force, but by 2023 he said it should not apply to children of parents who entered illegally: he keeps birth on the soil for others.

civil-disobedience-accept-penalty.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 14) faults Harvard protesters who wanted to escape punishment, saying the willingness to bear punishment for breaking rules is part of what makes civil disobedience heroic.

close-ties-china.rationale: Pledged to decouple from China, ban US business expansion there and 'declare independence' from China.

corporate-influence.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 13) says he does not like corporations influencing politics at all, whether through election spending or lobbying, and his 2021 Senate testimony warned against a 'one-dollar, one-vote' corporatocracy.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 10) wants preferences based on economic hardship rather than race, saying racial disparities should be addressed as a side effect of good policy, not as the goal, and rejects inherited group guilt.

death-penalty.rationale: He would resume executions for rare, exceptionally grave crimes, with an appropriate and ethical method.

democracy-best.rationale: Defends self-government despite potentially bad decisions.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 1, 10) says democracy is messy and beautiful because citizens disagree and thrives on dissent, and in 2023 he said he wants people who disagree with him and 'legitimate disagreement'.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 10) rejects DiAngelo's view that any practice producing poor outcomes for minorities must be racist, and ch. 12 says the way to stop racial discrimination is to stop discriminating by race.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Called the climate change agenda a 'hoax' and 'climate religion', saying it harms more Americans than climate change itself (while accepting fossil fuels contribute to warming).

elite-replacement.rationale: In the December 2023 debate he said the great replacement theory is 'not some grand right-wing conspiracy theory' but a basic statement of the Democratic Party's platform.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: In his 2024 Lex Fridman interview he said he is not saying we should stop supporting allies or providing security blankets, only that allies must pay their share (NATO 2% criticism); his most recent clear position keeps alliances, which wins over his earlier harder NATO talk.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Calls affirmative action a national cancer, pledged to repeal Executive Order 11246 and end it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 2) says the size of one's bank account has nothing to do with moral worth and that nothing makes Brahmins superior, and its principles call for ending discrimination by race, gender and other inherited traits.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Defends merit rather than demographic equity.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Rejects blood-based nationality for civic nationalism.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Repeatedly urged people to 'drill, frack and burn coal' and opposed the anticarbon framework.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Called nuclear the best carbon-free energy known and urged embracing it.

experts-over-public.rationale: Rejects technocrats restraining the democratic will.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His 2023 presidential campaign said he supports a 12% flat tax across the board, with deductions and loopholes eliminated.

force-without-un.rationale: Pledged to use the military, including drones, against Mexican drug cartels.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 11) accepts the Civil Rights Act's ban on private discrimination in jobs, housing and public accommodations, notes the market did not end Jim Crow discrimination, and proposes adding political belief as a protected category.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Supported broad restrictions on transgender Americans' rights and called for banning gender 'care' for minors.

gender-social-construct.rationale: In the August 2023 debate he listed 'there are two genders' among his core truths, and he repeatedly called transgenderism a mental health disorder.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Supports English proficiency among immigrant qualifications.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 11-12) mocks intersectionality as an unfalsifiable concept nobody understands and part of a woke catechism that must be accepted whole.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: In the November and December 2023 debates he praised the founding vision of Israel under Ben-Gurion and said Israel has an absolute right to defend itself without others second-guessing it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: In mid-2023 he called himself a 'path to legalization guy for a lot of different drugs' and backed federal marijuana legalization, but then denied backing decriminalization of hard drugs: his words point both ways.

limit-growth.rationale: Calls to 'grow our way out of problems', increase the supply of everything and unleash the economy; rejects the carbon framework.

limit-guns.rationale: Described as a Second Amendment absolutist who supports constitutional carry and wants to shut down the ATF.

local-veto-new-housing.rationale: In the November 2023 debate he said land-use restrictions constrict the housing supply and make homes more expensive, and called for increasing the supply of housing.

mandatory-environmental-reporting.rationale: In 2021 House testimony he urged Congress not to mandate climate and ESG disclosures, calling them a back-door route to climate policy, while allowing that some mandatory disclosures can be justified.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: In Woke, Inc. (ch. 2) he says capitalism organizes commercial life better than anything we could have imagined, and in the 2023 debates he called capitalism the best system known to lift people from poverty; he still wants corporate power fenced off from politics.

military-superiority.rationale: In the November 2023 debate he called for raising US naval capacity by at least 20% to meet AUKUS commitments and rebuilding the defense industrial base against China.

nation-first.rationale: Calls himself an 'America first' conservative who will not apologize for it.

national-rebirth.rationale: Platform calls for reviving American national identity and says the country has drifted into victimhood and mediocrity.

no-bailouts.rationale: He opposed bailouts for both SVB and its uninsured depositors, and preferred a private acquisition.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 1, 5, 9) attacks bailouts, corporate welfare, lobbied regulatory moats and Section 230 as crony capitalism, and in December 2023 he pledged to end the health insurers' antitrust exemption and vaccine makers' liability shield.

open-borders.rationale: Wants to use the military to secure the border and universally deport illegal immigrants.

patriotic-education.rationale: His 2026 ten-point platform calls for teaching kids to be proud of their state and country; flag and anthem are not mentioned.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Says Americans should embrace and be proud of their national identity and calls Judeo-Christian values the cornerstone of it; his platform pledges to 'revive American national identity'.

price-stability-first.rationale: In the 2023 debates he called for stabilizing the dollar and a new Federal Reserve chair who puts the priority on dollar stability.

prohibit-child-medical-transition.rationale: In the September and December 2023 debates he pledged to ban 'genital mutilation or chemical castration' for minors, using federal funding to make states comply.

property-fundamental.rationale: In the December 2023 debate he called the use of eminent domain to run a carbon-capture pipeline across Iowa farmland unconstitutional and wrong.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 3) says he does not believe in 'systemic racism' and sees it as an excuse for not fixing poverty and failing schools, though ch. 14 concedes systemic inequality exists through causes like long summer breaks.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Wants to seal the border, deport illegal immigrants, cut refugee admissions and favors a merit-based system, but defends the H-1B skilled visa programme.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Woke, Inc. says new regulation is self-defeating because big firms capture it and calls his liability proposals deregulation, yet he wants corporate liability shields narrowed, Big Tech bound by the First Amendment and, in 2023, crypto rules to catch up.

religious-nation.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 13, 15) says America is defined by a set of ideas rather than a single religion or ethnicity, and credits constitutional religious freedom with letting many faiths coexist.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Defends expression even of heinous opinions.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: In the November 2023 debate he said the US cannot keep 'sending foreign aid willy-nilly' to countries less indebted per head than itself; he did not address aid to the world's poorest directly.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Calls same-sex marriage settled precedent and said he has no negative view of same-sex couples, though he stops short of campaigning for it.

school-vouchers.rationale: Described as an advocate of school choice and government vouchers, and proposed giving federal education money directly to parents.

separate-church-state.rationale: Woke, Inc. (chs. 1-2) presents the separation of church and state as part of the American design worth protecting, alongside separating democracy from capitalism.

separated-powers.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 2) praises the Constitution's separation of powers among the branches, between federal and state governments and between church and state, and he cites separation of powers against agency tribunals in the 2024 Fridman interview.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: He called transgenderism a mental health disorder in the 2023 debates and listed 'there are two genders' as a basic truth, rejecting the view that sex categories are constructed.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He expressly opposed Biden’s student-loan bailouts, applying the same principle as to bank rescue.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 13) condemns blacklists of political opponents from McCarthy to today and says speech should be answered with more speech, contrasting the US with the Chinese Communist Party; in 2023 he opposed disbanding pro-Hamas student groups, urging 'leadership, not censorship'.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Woke, Inc. (ch. 9) speaks critically of the 'permanent new surveillance state' the military-industrial complex built after 9/11, likening it to Big Tech's censorship after January 6.

tax-inheritance.rationale: In Nation of Victims (2022) he wrote that inheritance taxes need 'real teeth', but his 2023 campaign replaced this with a 12% flat tax on all income including inheritances: his positions point both ways.

traditional-family.rationale: In the August 2023 debate he said 'the nuclear family is the greatest form of governance known to mankind' and tied the education crisis to fatherlessness.

unions-good.rationale: In the September 2023 debate he said he has sympathy for workers but no patience for union bosses, and in August 2023 he called for ending teachers unions at the local level.

vote-at-sixteen.rationale: In May 2023 he backed a constitutional amendment raising the voting age from 18 to 25, with service or a civics test as the way for younger adults to vote.

notes:
Positions shift over time (inheritance tax, immigration framing). Research relied on summaries and secondary coverage of his statements; his books were not available as full text.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 27 answers taken from it, 12 agreed, 1 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent pass; existing answers not read. Full 490-statement catalog and existing blanks reviewed. Long interviews searched across all themes, with latest Ohio commitments weighed against earlier federal proposals. No inference from party, business career or personal religious practice. The listed revolutionary Marxist propositions remain null. Democracy and consent are supported by explicit defenses of popular self-government; competitive multiparty elections by his express wish for substantive Democratic opponents. Constitutional adherence does not settle every institutional design question. Medicaid fraud reductions do not alone establish cutting legitimate welfare for dependency. Broad technology optimism, animal experimentation, tariffs, immigration levels and general drug legalization remain unknown. Rhetoric is never high confidence. Warrantless hunting searches do not settle the terrorism-surveillance question. Pollution tort enforcement does not exclude all agencies, and data-center conditions are too narrow to settle that choice. AI-assisted fraud detection is not replacement of government decision-making.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-11-07): read the maintainer-supplied full text of Woke, Inc. (2021), his 2021 House and Senate hearing testimony (local hearings corpus), and his own turns in the four 2023 GOP debate transcripts (American Presidency Project), plus targeted web checks. Brought to rules 4: every source tagged words (he holds no office, so there is no record). Answers that rested only on Wikipedia or OnTheIssues were re-sourced to his own words or nulled (collective-defense, voter-id), with the earlier versions kept in reviewHistory; legalize-drugs became 0 (cannabis legalization backed, hard-drug decriminalization disowned) and tax-inheritance 0 (2022 book vs 2023 flat tax). Themes searched: economy (taxes, Fed, regulation, patents, housing), government (separation of powers, voting age, corporate influence), society (family, race, gender), liberty (speech, surveillance, discrimination law), world (Israel, Ukraine, Taiwan, aid). The local corpora hold nothing else of his (no Congress record; Fridman #445 is outside the local set).
